cards.explanation: The answer is God. David says it plainly: "…for in You my soul takes refuge." He's in a cave with a king after him, and he still points straight at God. When I was stuck in that drawer, I would have taken any refuge going, so I admire a man who picks the best one.

The answer is until the danger has passed. David says, "In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed." Notice he doesn't say he's leaving early. He settles in and stays under there till the trouble is done. That's a man who knows where the good shade is.

The answer is that God fulfills His purpose for him. David cries out "…to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me." Even from a cave, he's sure God has a purpose for him and will carry it out. That's a lot of confidence for a man hiding from a king.

The answer is False. David says, "He reaches down from heaven and saves me…" God isn't stuck up in heaven watching from a distance. In the cave, David says God reaches down and rebukes those who trample him.

The answer is His loving devotion and His truth. David says, "…God sends forth His loving devotion and His truth." Right after talking about enemies, he talks about what God sends. I think that's a pretty good reply to trouble.

The answer is men. David says he lies down "…with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords." Those are his words for how sharp and cutting these men are. I think that's one tough crowd to be among.

The answer is, be exalted above the heavens. David says his soul is among the lions, and right there he says, "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth." He doesn't ask for his own safety there. He lifts his eyes to God's glory. That's some focus.
The answer is True. David says, "They dug a pit before me, but they themselves have fallen into it!" The pit they dug for him caught them instead. I think that's a plot twist worth a Selah.

The answer is sing and make music. David says, "My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music." A cave, a king hunting him, and he's planning a concert. I'd still be checking the cave for exits.
The answer is True. David says, "Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre!" The harp and lyre are the ones he calls on to wake up. I think that's a man ready to make music.

The answer is False. David says, "I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples." He's not keeping this song in the cave. He plans to sing it out loud among the nations.

The answer is to the heavens. David says, "For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens, and Your faithfulness to the clouds." That's his reason for singing among the peoples. Pretty high, friends.
